question.problem:
Consider the function $L:{R}^{3\times 2}\to R$ defined by $L(A)=(3Ax-2b)^{T}(3Ax-2b),$ where $$ x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]. $$ What is ${∇}_{A}L$ at $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]?$
${∇}_{A}=\,\,$ {{field-1}} $-96$
$0$ {{field-2}}
{{field-3}} $864$
question.worked_solution:
The gradient of $L$ with respect to $A$ is a matrix of the same shape as $A$, with $(i,j)$th entry given by

$$
\frac{∂L}{∂{a}_{ij}},
$$

the partial derivative of $L$ with respect to the $(i,j)$th entry of $A.$

We can compute $\frac{∂L}{∂{a}_{ij}}$ by applying the chain rule.

Let $y=3Ax-2b\in {R}^{3}.$ Then, $L(A)={y}^{T}y$ and

$$
\frac{∂L}{∂{a}_{ij}}={\sum }_{k=1}^{3}\frac{∂L}{∂{y}_{k}}\cdot \frac{∂{y}_{k}}{∂{a}_{ij}}
$$

Now, since 

$$
{∇}_{y}L={∇}_{y}({y}^{T}y)=2y,
$$

we have that

$$
\frac{∂L}{∂{y}_{k}}=2{y}_{k}.
$$

Writing out $y=3Ax-2b$ in component-wise notation as 

$$
{y}_{i}=3{\sum }_{j=1}^{2}{a}_{ij}{x}_{j}-2{b}_{i},
$$

we have 

- $\frac{∂{y}_{k}}{∂{a}_{ij}}=3{x}_{j}$ if $i=k$, and

- $\frac{∂{y}_{k}}{∂{a}_{ij}}=0$ if $i\ne k.$

This means that 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂L}{∂{a}_{ij}} & ={\sum }_{k=1}^{3}\frac{∂L}{∂{y}_{k}}\cdot \frac{∂{y}_{k}}{∂{a}_{ij}} \\  & =\frac{∂L}{∂{y}_{i}}\cdot \frac{∂{y}_{i}}{∂{a}_{ij}} \\  & =2{y}_{i}\cdot \frac{∂{y}_{i}}{∂{a}_{ij}} \\  & =2{y}_{i}\cdot 3{x}_{j} \\  & =6{y}_{i}{x}_{j}.\end{aligned}
$$

The $(i,j)$th entry of ${∇}_{A}L$ is $6$ times the $i$th entry of $y$ multiplied by the $j$th entry of $x$, so

$$
{∇}_{A}L=6y\cdot {x}^{T}.
$$

Finally, evaluating ${∇}_{A}L$ at $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}],$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∇}_{A}L & =6y\cdot {x}^{T} \\  & =6(3Ax-2b)\cdot {x}^{T} \\  & =6(3[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}])\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =6(3[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 8 \\ 12\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}])\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-24 \\ 132 \\ 216\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -96 \\ 0 & 528 \\ 0 & 864\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
